programs.title: Observing Europe-So many UK Prime Ministers, same old problems
programs.desc: Since moving to London, CGTN's Li Jianhua has witnessed the UK cycle through four leaders. In this video, Jianhua reflects on the problems facing each of those prime ministers… and why it's affected how he buys grapes.

programs.title: Observing Europe-Who owns Britain?
programs.desc: One of the first things that surprised CGTN's Li Jianhua after moving to Britain was discovering that London’s iconic black cabs are made by a subsidiary of China’s Geely. It’s not alone. Jaguar Land Rover belongs to India’s Tata, Mini is owned by Germany’s BMW, and many of Britain’s airports, utilities and landmark buildings have foreign owners. For decades, Britain embraced global investment. But the battle over British Steel suggests attitudes are changing. As concerns grow around national security and economic resilience, the question is no longer just who invests in Britain — but which industries are too strategic to be foreign-owned. In this latest episode of his series Observing Europe, Jianhua explores ownership, investment – and where Britain is drawing the line.

programs.title: Observing Europe - Is migration "weaponized" in Europe?
programs.desc: Schengen - one of Europe’s greatest achievements - is being tested. The Schengen Area promised border-free travel across much of Europe. But migration, security concerns and increasingly polarized politics are putting that promise under pressure. From Ceuta to the return of internal border checks, CGTN Europe correspondent Li Jianhua looks at how Europe’s migration debate is reshaping Schengen — and asks: Can Europe keep its internal borders open as political pressure to control migration grows?

programs.title: BizTalk | AI-powered travel reshaping global tourism
programs.desc: China’s tourism market has continued to heat up this summer. Behind this boom, artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how people travel and is opening up new opportunities for the industry – from personalized itineraries to immersive experiences. In this episode of BizTalk, guests from the World Economic Forum, the World Travel & Tourism Council and Atout France explore how smart technologies can enhance visitor experiences, optimize destination management and unlock new growth opportunities. They also examine what China's emerging "AI tourism" focus could offer the global tourism industry.

programs.title: Meet China: When Chinese Dynamism Reshapes Landscapes — Boundless Challenges, Infinite Vitality
programs.desc: In this episode of Meet China, we journey from the cloud-piercing peaks of Zhangjiajie to the tech-driven streets of Shenzhen and the cassava farms of Vietnam. We meet extreme athletes redefining personal limits, turning vertical cliffs and open skies into new playgrounds. Then, we ride in a fully autonomous robotaxi through Shenzhen traffic, exploring the technology and regulations accelerating the global race for self-driving cars. Finally, we travel to Vietnam, where Chinese investment and expertise have transformed the cassava industry—boosting yields, stabilizing farmer incomes, and creating resilient supply chains reaching global markets. From skies to roads to fields, this episode shows how China’s dynamism is reshaping landscapes and lives worldwide.

programs.title: Summer Davos 2026: The Future of Jobs, Skills, and Sustainable Growth
programs.desc: Global trade is undergoing profound change as economies grapple with shifting supply chains, rapid advances in artificial intelligence, and the transition to cleaner energy. We are coming to you from the Summer Davos Forum in Dalian, where policymakers, business leaders, and academics from around the world are discussing how to navigate these transformations. One key question at this year's forum is how these changes will affect workers, and whether they will create new opportunities or deepen existing challenges. To discuss the future of jobs, skills, and sustainable growth, Song Ruixin is joined by Professor Mercedes Maroto-Valer, Deputy Principal for Global Sustainability at Heriot-Watt University, and Kathleen Alexander, co-founder and CEO of Savor, a San Jose based food startup.

programs.title: Zhejiang transforms technology into market success
programs.desc: East China's Zhejiang Province has long been known for its strong private-sector economy and vibrant business environment. Now, it's putting that market-driven approach to work in next-generation technology, helping turn lab innovations into real-world products. CGTN reporter Wang Tianyu reports from Zhejiang.

programs.title: The village workshops giving rural residents a new choice in Zhejiang
programs.desc: For millions of Chinese workers, earning more has often meant leaving home. But one village in Zhejiang is trying to change that. A local workshop is bringing jobs closer to home. CGTN reporter Yu Bokun sees how it is creating new opportunities.

programs.title: How China turns humble loofah plants into premium bath products
programs.desc: A simple loofah can become a premium bath or kitchen product worth more than $10. Behind that transformation is a partnership between Huangmei in Hubei and Ningbo — one provides the land and labor, the other the technology and markets. CGTN's Yu Bokun finds out how this humble crop goes global.

programs.title: Follow the Money: Where Climate Capital Is Going
programs.desc: Clean energy investment has surpassed fossil fuel supply investment, signaling a fundamental shift in how markets address climate risk. Capital is accelerating into renewables, electrification, and industrial decarbonization—but how do we ensure these funds drive climate action? CGTN's Guan Xin moderates a panel at the 2026 Summer Davos Forum, bringing together voices from government, business, and international institutions to explore the trends, challenges, and prospects of climate capital allocation. Tune in to find out where climate capital is flowing and explore the opportunities in the green transition.#SummerDavos2026
